title: Resolution-column quasi-isomorphisms of the pushed-forward Cech complex
statement: Let $f:X'\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $U=(U_i)_{i\in I}$ any family of open subsets of $X$, $A^\bullet$ a complex of injective $\mathcal O_{X'}$-modules in degrees $\mathbf N$, and $K^\bullet$ a complex of injective $\mathcal O_X$-modules in degrees $\mathbf N$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. For every quasi-isomorphism $\lambda:f_*A^\bullet\to K^\bullet$ [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] and every Cech degree $q$, the resolution-direction column of $\check C(U,\lambda)$ [def-sc-cech-complex-augmentations] is a quasi-isomorphism. This column is the degree-$q$ component of the flipped bicomplex map. No covering or quasi-coherence condition is required.

proof.text: For each tuple y, use the categorical finite-product open V(y) appearing in the Cech functor. Its sections functor S(y) is additive and left exact. module_pushforward_injective_acyclic supplies S(y)-acyclicity of every source term; rightAcyclic_of_injective supplies that of every target term. Apply Functor.quasiIso_map_of_rightAcyclic_nat to lambda, obtaining a quasi-isomorphism of module-valued section complexes on V(y).

Restrict the scalars of the sections at V(y) to the global section ring. Restriction of scalars is exact and preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Assemble these functors into an additive functor T to diagrams indexed by the discrete category of (q+1)-tuples. HomologicalComplex.quasiIso_iff_evaluation proves that T(lambda) is a quasi-isomorphism from the coordinatewise assertions.

The global module category satisfies Mathlib AB4Star, so lim on discrete tuple diagrams is exact and preserves homology. Therefore applying lim termwise to T(lambda) gives a quasi-isomorphism. The resulting objects, differentials and map components are definitionally those of degree q in the flipped moduleCechDoubleFunctor map. This proves the claimed QuasiIso directly, including empty tuple sets and empty product opens.

mathlib_searches.results: Eight results, including InjectiveResolution.desc_commutes and Hom.ι_comp_hom. No arbitrary-complex Cech augmentation or pushed-forward tuple-total naturality theorem.
Twelve ShortComplex results about preservation of homology and componentwise isomorphisms. No Cech refinement theorem.

Mathlib refinement matches concern Stone-Cech compactification. Library ModuleCechLiftSquares proves squares only for two injective resolutions. cupCechDouble gives the same termwise object but no arbitrary-complex augmentation API. FirstQuadrantTotalComparison gives total comparison, not sectionwise acyclicity or refinement. Blueprint search for Cech refinement, Cech quasi-isomorphism and 01FD gives no imported blueprint node.

theorem cech_pushforward_lambda_columns {X X' : Scheme.{v}} (f : X' ⟶ X)
    {ι : Type v} (U : ι → X.Opens) (A : CochainComplex X'.Modules ℕ)
    (K : CochainComplex X.Modules ℕ)
    (hA : ∀ n : ℕ, Injective (A.X n)) (hK : ∀ n : ℕ, Injective (K.X n))
    (l : ((pushforward f).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj A ⟶ K)
    (hl : QuasiIso l) (q : ℕ) :
    QuasiIso (((HomologicalComplex₂.flipFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} Γ(X, ⊤))
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ) (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).map
        ((moduleCechDoubleFunctor U).map l)).f q)
